name: Qatar
main_industries: Oil & Gas · Finance · Construction · Tourism
summary: High income market with strong government investment pipeline
key_industry_1_desc: Qatar is the worlds largest LNG exporter. North Field expansion will increase capacity by 60% by 2027.
key_industry_2_desc: Qatar Financial Centre hosts 1,000+ firms. QIA sovereign wealth fund of $450B drives significant investment activity.
key_industry_3_desc: Post-World Cup legacy infrastructure development continues. Smart city and urban development projects active.
key_industry_4_desc: Qatar targeting 6M visitors annually by 2030. Strong investment in luxury tourism and business events infrastructure.
talent_overview: Qatar workforce is 95% expatriate. English is the business language. Strong Indian, Filipino and Arab professional community.
talent_localisation_rule: Qatarisation targets apply in financial services and government sectors. Private sector targets are sector specific.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit required and employer sponsored. New labour reforms introduced portability allowing job changes.
talent_key_consideration: Qatar abolished the kafala sponsorship system in 2020 giving workers more mobility than most GCC markets.
sector_priority_1_why: North Field expansion creating massive supply chain and technology partnership opportunities for international energy firms.
sector_priority_2_why: QFC offers 100% foreign ownership, 10% corporate tax and a common law framework attractive to financial institutions.
sector_priority_3_why: Post-World Cup momentum and National Tourism Strategy 2030 creating strong hotel and hospitality investment pipeline.
entry_playbook_overview: Qatar offers two main entry routes — onshore via commercial registration or through Qatar Financial Centre for financial and professional services.
entry_step_1: Choose your entry route — QFC for financial and professional services, onshore commercial registration for other sectors
entry_step_2: Obtain commercial registration — Ministry of Commerce and Industry is the primary registration authority
entry_step_3: Register with General Tax Authority — Corporate tax registration required for all operating entities
entry_step_4: Secure office space and obtain municipal licences — Physical presence required for most business licences
geopolitical_alert: Defensive action required against regional strikes. LNG exports exposed to Hormuz closure.
current_conditions_summary: Significantly impaired. Qatar has been required to take defensive action against missile and drone activity, and its LNG export capability is directly exposed to the Strait of Hormuz closure. As a small, trade-dependent economy hosting major foreign military infrastructure, exposure is concentrated.
current_conditions_factors: Direct exposure to missile and drone activity; LNG export dependency on Hormuz; hosts major foreign military infrastructure; small landmass limits dispersal; elevated insurance and security costs
current_conditions_outlook: Long-term fundamentals — wealth, infrastructure, regulatory openness — are not diminished. Near-term entry is difficult to justify except where there is an existing commitment or a compelling strategic reason. Defer new physical presence pending de-escalation.

name: Kuwait
main_industries: Oil & Gas · Finance · Real Estate · Retail
summary: Oil-rich economy with growing private sector diversification
key_industry_1_desc: Kuwait holds 6% of global oil reserves. KPC manages upstream and downstream operations with significant expansion plans.
key_industry_2_desc: Kuwait is home to one of the worlds largest sovereign wealth funds at $800B+ managed by Kuwait Investment Authority.
key_industry_3_desc: Kuwait Vision 2035 New Kuwait plan driving infrastructure investment in transport, housing and public facilities.
key_industry_4_desc: Government investing heavily in private healthcare capacity. Medical city projects creating significant PPP opportunities.
talent_overview: Kuwait workforce is 80% expatriate. Arabic is the official language but English widely used in business.
talent_localisation_rule: Kuwaitisation quotas apply across private sector. Financial sector requires 60% Kuwaiti nationals in senior roles.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit and residency visa required. Employer sponsored. Process can take 6 to 12 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Public sector is heavily preferred by Kuwaiti nationals making private sector Kuwaitisation challenging in practice.
sector_priority_1_why: KPC expansion programme creating significant demand for oilfield services, technology and engineering firms.
sector_priority_2_why: Government PPP programme opening significant opportunities for private healthcare operators and medical technology firms.
sector_priority_3_why: New Kuwait 2035 plan committing billions to transport, housing and utilities infrastructure development.
entry_playbook_overview: Kuwait requires foreign firms to have a local Kuwaiti agent or partner for most commercial activities outside free zones.
entry_step_1: Identify a local Kuwaiti agent or partner — required for most government and commercial tender participation
entry_step_2: Register with Ministry of Commerce — obtain commercial licence through MOOCI single window system
entry_step_3: Register with Kuwait Tax Authority — corporate tax applies to foreign company shares of profits
entry_step_4: Register for Kuwait social insurance — required for all employees including expatriates in certain categories
geopolitical_alert: Critical infrastructure damage reported. Among the most heavily targeted regional states.
current_conditions_summary: Most severely affected GCC market. Kuwait has been among the most heavily targeted states in the region, with confirmed damage to critical utilities infrastructure including power generation and water desalination. Essential service continuity cannot currently be assumed.
current_conditions_factors: Heaviest strike exposure in the GCC; confirmed damage to power and desalination infrastructure; utility continuity risk; Hormuz export dependency; proximity to conflict zone; staff safety concerns
current_conditions_outlook: Structural fundamentals persist but are not the operative consideration right now. New market entry is not advisable until infrastructure continuity and security stabilise. Existing operators should prioritise contingency and staff welfare planning.

name: Bahrain
main_industries: Finance · Fintech · Manufacturing · Tourism · Logistics
summary: Most open GCC economy with strong fintech and financial services
key_industry_1_desc: Bahrain is the GCCs most open financial market. CBB regulates a mature ecosystem of banks, insurers and fintechs.
key_industry_2_desc: Bahrain is a regional cloud hub hosting AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud MEA infrastructure.
key_industry_3_desc: ALBA is one of the worlds largest aluminium smelters. Manufacturing sector contributes 14% of GDP.
key_industry_4_desc: Bahrain Tourism and Exhibitions Authority targeting 14M visitors annually. Strong weekend tourism from Saudi Arabia.
talent_overview: Bahrain has the most liberal labour market in the GCC. Workers can change jobs without employer permission under flexi-permit system.
talent_localisation_rule: Bahrainisation targets range from 5% in oil sector to 50% in retail. Financial sector has specific CBB requirements.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit via Labour Market Regulatory Authority. Flexi-permit available for self-sponsored workers.
talent_key_consideration: Bahrain offers the most flexible labour mobility in the GCC making it attractive for firms needing workforce agility.
sector_priority_1_why: CBB regulatory sandbox and 0% tax environment make Bahrain the most accessible GCC market for fintech firms.
sector_priority_2_why: Bahrain Cloud First policy and major hyperscaler presence creating strong demand for cloud services and solutions.
sector_priority_3_why: Khalifa Bin Salman Port expansion and proximity to Saudi Arabia creating strong logistics and distribution opportunities.
entry_playbook_overview: Bahrain is the fastest and most straightforward GCC market to enter. 100% foreign ownership permitted across most sectors.
entry_step_1: Register via Sijilaat — Bahrains one-stop online business registration portal. Process takes 1 to 3 days
entry_step_2: Obtain sector specific licences — CBB licence for financial services, other regulators for relevant sectors
entry_step_3: Open corporate bank account — Bahrain has a mature banking sector with straightforward KYC processes
entry_step_4: Register with National Bureau for Revenue — VAT registration required if turnover exceeds BHD 37,500
geopolitical_alert: Defensive action required against regional strikes. Elevated exposure profile.
current_conditions_summary: Severely affected. Bahrain has been required to take defensive action against regional strikes, and hosts significant foreign naval infrastructure that increases its exposure profile. Its small size and heavy dependence on regional trade and financial flows compound the impact.
current_conditions_factors: Direct exposure to regional strikes; hosts major foreign naval infrastructure; very small landmass; dependence on regional financial and trade flows; Hormuz proximity; causeway and logistics disruption risk
current_conditions_outlook: Bahrain's regulatory openness and financial-services positioning remain structurally sound. Near-term entry should be deferred; the risk-reward does not currently favour new physical commitment.

name: Oman
main_industries: Oil & Gas · Logistics · Tourism · Fisheries · Manufacturing
summary: Stable and diversifying economy with logistics strengths
key_industry_1_desc: PDO is the main oil producer. Oman LNG exports to Asia are a key revenue source. Block exploration ongoing.
key_industry_2_desc: Port of Salalah and Sohar Industrial Port are major regional logistics hubs with significant expansion underway.
key_industry_3_desc: Oman Vision 2040 targets tourism as a major GDP contributor. Natural, cultural and adventure tourism are priorities.
key_industry_4_desc: Special Economic Zones at Duqm and Sohar offering competitive incentives for industrial and manufacturing investment.
talent_overview: Oman has a young national workforce with universities producing 40,000 graduates annually. English widely used in business.
talent_localisation_rule: Omanisation quotas range from 15% in industry to 60% in financial services. Enforced by Ministry of Labour.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work visa required and employer sponsored. Integrated visa system managed through Ministry of Labour portal.
talent_key_consideration: Oman is investing heavily in vocational training to improve national workforce readiness for private sector roles.
sector_priority_1_why: Duqm SEZ and Sohar Port offer competitive incentives and strategic location between Asia, Africa and Europe.
sector_priority_2_why: Underdeveloped tourism sector relative to regional peers creating first mover advantage for hotel and hospitality investors.
sector_priority_3_why: Oman targeting 30% renewable energy by 2030 with major solar and green hydrogen projects in development.
entry_playbook_overview: Oman offers straightforward market entry via the Invest Easy portal. Special Economic Zones offer enhanced incentives.
entry_step_1: Register via Invest Easy portal — Omans online one stop shop for business registration and licencing
entry_step_2: Consider SEZ locations — Duqm, Sohar and Salalah offer tax holidays and 100% foreign ownership
entry_step_3: Register with Oman Tax Authority — corporate income tax at 15% applies to most businesses
entry_step_4: Develop Omanisation plan — submit workforce localisation plan to Ministry of Labour before hiring
geopolitical_alert: Hormuz frontage disrupted. Defensive action required against regional activity.
current_conditions_summary: Substantially affected but comparatively better positioned. Oman has been required to take defensive action, and its Strait of Hormuz frontage places it at the centre of the shipping disruption. Its longstanding neutral diplomatic posture may moderate some direct exposure relative to neighbours.
current_conditions_factors: Hormuz frontage and shipping disruption; defensive action required; regional trade dependency; neutral diplomatic posture as partial mitigant; elevated insurance costs; tourism and logistics impact
current_conditions_outlook: Oman's structural position and diplomatic neutrality mean it may recover faster than more directly involved neighbours. Still not a market for new physical commitment right now, but worth monitoring closely for early re-entry signals.

name: United Arab Emirates
main_industries: Oil & Gas · Finance · Tourism · Real Estate · Logistics
summary: Regional hub with 100% foreign ownership in free zones
key_industry_1_desc: DIFC is the regions premier financial hub hosting 5,000+ firms including global banks, asset managers and insurers.
key_industry_2_desc: Dubai welcomed 17M+ international visitors in 2023. Luxury, MICE and medical tourism are priority growth areas.
key_industry_3_desc: Jebel Ali is the worlds 9th largest port. UAE sits at the crossroads of Asia, Africa and Europe trade routes.
key_industry_4_desc: UAE targets 44% clean energy by 2050. Masdar City and DEWA projects are driving massive investment.
talent_overview: UAE workforce is 89% expatriate. English is the business language. Talent pool is large, diverse and internationally mobile.
talent_localisation_rule: Emiratisation applies to private sector firms with 50+ employees. Targets increase annually across skilled roles.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Employment visa required. Sponsored by employer. Process typically takes 2 to 4 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Competition for senior talent is intense. Compensation packages typically include housing, schooling and flights.
sector_priority_1_why: DIFC and ADGM offer world class regulatory frameworks with 0% tax and 100% foreign ownership for financial firms.
sector_priority_2_why: UAE Net Zero 2050 strategy is driving billions in solar, hydrogen and clean tech investment opportunities.
sector_priority_3_why: Ageing expat population and medical tourism ambition driving strong demand for healthcare infrastructure and services.
entry_playbook_overview: UAE offers two primary entry routes — mainland and free zone — each with distinct ownership, tax and operational implications.
entry_step_1: Choose your structure — Free zone for 100% ownership and tax benefits, or Mainland for broader market access
entry_step_2: Select your jurisdiction — Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah each offer different free zones suited to different sectors
entry_step_3: Obtain your trade licence — Commercial, professional or industrial licence depending on activity
entry_step_4: Open corporate bank account — Allow 4 to 8 weeks. Requires full KYC documentation and business plan
geopolitical_alert: Strait of Hormuz closed. Regional conflict directly affecting trade routes and logistics.
current_conditions_summary: Severely affected. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz directly disrupts the UAE's role as a regional trade and re-export hub, with Jebel Ali throughput and supply chains under acute pressure. Regional airspace and shipping insurance costs have risen sharply. Business continuity planning is now a prerequisite for any new market entry.
current_conditions_factors: Strait of Hormuz closure; elevated shipping and aviation insurance; regional airspace disruption; expatriate workforce departure risk; supply chain re-routing costs
current_conditions_outlook: Structural fundamentals remain intact and the long-term case is unchanged. Near-term entry should be staged, with contingency planning for logistics and staff mobility. Reassess as the Hormuz situation develops.

name: Pakistan
main_industries: Agriculture · Textiles · Remittances · IT Services · Manufacturing
summary: 230M population market with significant macro challenges
key_industry_1_desc: Pakistan is worlds 4th largest cotton producer and major garment exporter. Textile sector employs 40% of industrial workforce.
key_industry_2_desc: Agriculture contributes 24% of GDP. Pakistan is a major exporter of rice, cotton, wheat and sugarcane.
key_industry_3_desc: Pakistan exports $2.6B in IT services. Karachi and Lahore are growing tech hubs with strong freelance developer community.
key_industry_4_desc: CPEC energy projects have added 10,000MW of capacity. Renewable energy is a growing priority under IMF programme.
talent_overview: Pakistan has a young population with 64% under 30. English widely used in business. Strong IT and engineering talent at competitive cost.
talent_localisation_rule: No formal localisation quota outside of some sectors. Companies expected to prioritise local hiring as general practice.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit required from Ministry of Interior. Employer sponsored. Process can take 8 to 16 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Pakistan offers some of the most cost competitive English speaking IT talent globally making it attractive for technology outsourcing.
sector_priority_1_why: PSEB support, competitive talent costs and strong English proficiency making Pakistan increasingly attractive for IT outsourcing.
sector_priority_2_why: Large agricultural base with low processing value add creating significant opportunity for food technology and processing investment.
sector_priority_3_why: Pakistan solar and wind potential is among South Asias highest. Government AEDB incentives support renewable project development.
entry_playbook_overview: Pakistan market entry requires careful planning given macro instability. SECP registration is straightforward but FX and repatriation planning is critical.
entry_step_1: Register with SECP — Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan online portal for company incorporation
entry_step_2: Register with FBR — Federal Board of Revenue for NTN national tax number and sales tax registration
entry_step_3: Open PKR and USD accounts — establish banking relationships with HBL, UBL or MCB before commencing operations
entry_step_4: Register with BOI — Board of Investment for foreign investment facilitation and repatriation approval processes
current_conditions_summary: No significant current geopolitical factors affecting this market beyond normal business risk considerations.
current_conditions_factors: Normal business environment · Standard regulatory monitoring · No elevated conflict exposure
current_conditions_outlook: Current conditions broadly consistent with structural fundamentals. Standard market entry timing considerations apply.

name: Philippines
main_industries: BPO & IT Services · Remittances · Manufacturing · Agriculture · Tourism
summary: English speaking BPO powerhouse with young population and strong digital economy growth
highlight_1: Largest English speaking BPO hub in Asia
highlight_2: Strong remittance inflows providing economic stability
highlight_3: Young demographic dividend with median age of 25
key_industry_1_desc: Philippines is the worlds BPO capital generating $32B+ annually. Over 1.3M workers serve US, UK and Australian clients across voice and non-voice services.
key_industry_2_desc: Overseas Filipino Workers send $36B+ annually making Philippines top 5 globally for remittances. Digital banking and fintech growing rapidly.
key_industry_3_desc: Philippines is a major electronics exporter particularly semiconductors. Laguna and Cavite provinces host significant Japanese and US manufacturing.
key_industry_4_desc: Philippines has 7,000+ islands with world class beaches and diving. Government targeting 12M visitors by 2028 with major resort development underway.
talent_overview: Philippines has one of Asias strongest English speaking talent pools with 500,000+ university graduates annually. Strong affinity for US business culture.
talent_localisation_rule: Foreign equity restrictions apply in several sectors. Retail, media and education have Filipino ownership requirements under Foreign Investment Negative List.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Alien Employment Permit required from DOLE for foreign workers. Process takes 3 to 6 weeks. 9G working visa required.
talent_key_consideration: Philippines offers the best English speaking talent at the most competitive cost in Asia making it ideal for customer service, finance and technology outsourcing.
sector_priority_1_why: PEZA registered BPO operations get 4 to 8 year income tax holidays and 5% GIT thereafter making Philippines the most cost effective English BPO destination.
sector_priority_2_why: Philippines has exceptional wind and solar resources. Retail competition market and green energy auction programme creating significant investment pipeline.
sector_priority_3_why: Government Build Better More infrastructure programme and tourism master plan creating significant construction and hospitality investment opportunities.
entry_playbook_overview: Philippines offers PEZA and BOI registered investment routes both offering significant tax incentives. PEZA is most popular for BPO and export oriented manufacturing.
entry_step_1: Choose investment registration — PEZA for export oriented BPO and manufacturing, BOI for domestic market oriented businesses
entry_step_2: Register with SEC — Securities and Exchange Commission for corporate registration. Check Foreign Investment Negative List for ownership restrictions in your sector
entry_step_3: Register with BIR — Bureau of Internal Revenue for tax identification number, VAT and withholding tax registration
entry_step_4: Obtain PEZA or BOI registration — apply for fiscal incentives including income tax holidays before commencing operations
current_conditions_summary: No significant current geopolitical factors affecting this market beyond normal business risk considerations.
current_conditions_factors: Normal business environment · Standard regulatory monitoring · No elevated conflict exposure
current_conditions_outlook: Current conditions broadly consistent with structural fundamentals. Standard market entry timing considerations apply.

name: Saudi Arabia
main_industries: Oil & Gas · Construction · Finance · Tourism · Technology
summary: Largest GCC economy undergoing rapid Vision 2030 reforms
key_industry_1_desc: Saudi Aramco is the worlds most profitable company. Vision 2030 is diversifying downstream petrochemical value chain.
key_industry_2_desc: NEOM, Red Sea Project, Diriyah and Qiddiya represent over $1 trillion in giga-project construction pipeline.
key_industry_3_desc: Saudi Arabia targeting 150M visitors by 2030. Massive investment in culture, sport and entertainment sectors.
key_industry_4_desc: Saudi Vision 2030 targets technology sector contribution of 3% of GDP. Cloud, AI and cybersecurity are priorities.
talent_overview: Saudi workforce of 15M with growing female participation now at 33%. English widely spoken in business contexts.
talent_localisation_rule: Nitaqat Saudisation programme mandates local hiring quotas ranging from 10% to 35% depending on sector and company size.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Iqama work permit required. Employer sponsored. Dependent on Nitaqat compliance status of the hiring company.
talent_key_consideration: Regional Headquarters mandate requires multinationals to employ Saudi nationals in senior leadership roles.
sector_priority_1_why: Over $1 trillion in committed project spend across NEOM, Red Sea, Diriyah creating enormous demand for contractors and consultants.
sector_priority_2_why: Government targeting 150M visitors by 2030 creating massive hotel, entertainment and transport infrastructure demand.
sector_priority_3_why: SDAIA and STZA are offering significant incentives for technology firms establishing regional operations in Saudi Arabia.
entry_playbook_overview: Saudi Arabia requires foreign firms to obtain a MISA licence. Multinationals bidding on government contracts must establish a Regional HQ.
entry_step_1: Obtain MISA licence — Ministry of Investment Saudi Arabia is the single window for foreign investment approvals
entry_step_2: Determine RHQ requirement — Mandatory for multinationals seeking government contracts from January 2024
entry_step_3: Register with ZATCA — Saudi tax authority registration required before commencing operations
entry_step_4: Establish Nitaqat compliance plan — Map your Saudisation targets by role before hiring begins
geopolitical_alert: Active regional conflict. Export routes and project delivery affected.
current_conditions_summary: Materially deteriorated. Saudi Arabia is directly involved in the regional conflict, and hydrocarbon export routes through the Strait of Hormuz are disrupted. Giga-project timelines face further pressure, and foreign staff mobility and insurance costs have risen significantly.
current_conditions_factors: Direct conflict involvement; Hormuz export disruption; giga-project delivery risk; elevated security and insurance costs; expatriate mobility constraints; oil revenue volatility
current_conditions_outlook: The structural case — open ownership, RHQ incentives, non-oil diversification — is unchanged and remains strong. However, current conditions argue against full-scale commitment. Structure and plan now; stage physical build-out.

name: Egypt
main_industries: Tourism · Oil & Gas · Remittances · Manufacturing · Agriculture
summary: Largest Arab economy with 100M+ consumer market
key_industry_1_desc: Egypt is a significant natural gas producer. Zohr field is Mediterraneans largest. Renewable energy pipeline is growing.
key_industry_2_desc: Egypt targets 30M visitors by 2028. Antiquities, Red Sea resorts and new mega-projects are driving investment.
key_industry_3_desc: Egypt is building an industrial manufacturing base in automotive, textiles and food processing targeting African exports.
key_industry_4_desc: Egypt has 100M+ population with low banking penetration creating significant fintech and digital finance opportunity.
talent_overview: Egypt has one of Africas largest talent pools with 700,000+ university graduates annually. Arabic is primary business language.
talent_localisation_rule: Egyptian Labour Law requires minimum 90% Egyptian nationals in company workforce. Exceptions apply for specialist roles.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit required from Ministry of Manpower. Quota based on company size. Process takes 4 to 8 weeks.
talent_key_consideration: Egypt offers highly cost competitive professional talent, particularly in engineering, IT and finance.
sector_priority_1_why: Egypt targets 42% renewable energy by 2030. Benban solar park and wind projects creating significant investment pipeline.
sector_priority_2_why: New administrative capital and Red Sea resort developments creating significant hotel and hospitality investment demand.
sector_priority_3_why: Central Bank of Egypt fintech sandbox and 60M+ unbanked population creating significant digital finance opportunity.
entry_playbook_overview: Egypt offers multiple entry structures. General Authority for Investment is the primary entry point for foreign investors.
entry_step_1: Register with GAFI — General Authority for Investment and Free Zones is the one stop shop for foreign investors
entry_step_2: Choose your structure — LLC is most common. Free zone options available for export oriented businesses
entry_step_3: Register with Egyptian Tax Authority — corporate tax at 22.5% applies. VAT registration required above threshold
entry_step_4: Open EGP and USD bank accounts — dual currency accounts essential given FX management requirements
geopolitical_alert: Egypt faces indirect exposure through Suez Canal disruptions linked to Red Sea Houthi activity. Canal revenue and tourism have been impacted. Monitor trade route situation closely.
current_conditions_summary: Suez Canal revenue significantly impacted by Red Sea Houthi activity linked to regional conflict. Tourism and FX stability also affected.
current_conditions_factors: Suez Canal revenue down 60% · Red Sea shipping diversions · Tourism impact · FX pressure continuing
current_conditions_outlook: Egypt facing meaningful economic headwinds from regional conflict. Canal revenue loss is significant. Monitor IMF programme compliance and FX stability closely.

name: Turkey
main_industries: Manufacturing · Tourism · Finance · Agriculture · Defence
summary: Bridge between Europe and Middle East with large domestic market
key_industry_1_desc: Turkey produces 1.4M vehicles annually. Ford, Fiat, Toyota and Renault have major manufacturing plants.
key_industry_2_desc: Turkey welcomed 57M visitors in 2023 making it the 4th most visited country globally. Revenue exceeded $54B.
key_industry_3_desc: Istanbul is a regional financial hub. Turkish banking sector is large with $1T+ in assets despite currency challenges.
key_industry_4_desc: Turkey is a top 10 global defence exporter. Bayraktar drones and indigenous fighter jets reflect growing defence capability.
talent_overview: Turkey has 35M strong workforce with strong engineering and manufacturing skills. Turkish is business language with English in multinationals.
talent_localisation_rule: Minimum 1 Turkish national per 5 foreign employees. Some sectors have specific requirements. Applied by Ministry of Labour.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Work permit from Ministry of Labour required. Employer sponsored. Process takes 4 to 8 weeks for approval.
talent_key_consideration: Turkey offers strong manufacturing and engineering talent at competitive European cost levels making it attractive for industrial investment.
sector_priority_1_why: Organised Industrial Zones offer competitive incentives for manufacturing investment targeting EU export markets.
sector_priority_2_why: Growing visitor numbers and undersupply of quality hospitality infrastructure creating investment opportunity across the country.
sector_priority_3_why: Turkey targeting 30% renewable energy by 2030. Solar and wind tender pipeline is one of the largest in the region.
entry_playbook_overview: Turkey has a straightforward company registration process. Investment Office of the Presidency provides facilitation for significant investments.
entry_step_1: Register with MERSİS — central trade registry system for company incorporation. Process takes 1 to 3 days
entry_step_2: Register with tax office — obtain tax number from local tax office before commencing any business activity
entry_step_3: Register with SGK — Social Security Institution for employee registration and social security contributions
entry_step_4: Consider OIZ location — Organised Industrial Zones offer VAT exemptions, subsidised utilities and streamlined permits
geopolitical_alert: Turkey is navigating complex diplomatic relationships with all parties. While not directly involved, trade routes and energy imports may be affected by broader regional escalation.
current_conditions_summary: Turkey navigating complex relationships with all conflict parties. Trade route impacts and energy import costs creating economic headwinds.
current_conditions_factors: Complex diplomatic positioning · Energy import cost pressure · Trade route disruption · Currency under pressure
current_conditions_outlook: Turkey attempting to leverage mediator role but economic exposure is real. Monitor lira stability and inflation trajectory alongside regional developments.

name: Nigeria
main_industries: Oil & Gas · Fintech · Agriculture · Telecoms · Entertainment
summary: Africas largest economy with high growth and high complexity
key_industry_1_desc: Nigeria is Africas fintech capital. Lagos hosts Flutterwave, Paystack and 200+ fintechs serving the continents largest unbanked population.
key_industry_2_desc: Nigeria is Africas largest oil producer. Dangote Refinery now operational transforming domestic refining capacity.
key_industry_3_desc: MTN, Airtel and Glo serve 200M+ subscribers. Data demand is surging driving infrastructure investment.
key_industry_4_desc: Nigeria is Africas largest agricultural economy. Government prioritising food processing to reduce imports.
talent_overview: Nigeria has Africas largest talent pool with 250M population and strong English language proficiency. Tech talent particularly strong.
talent_localisation_rule: Nigerian Content Act requires minimum local content in oil and gas sector. Other sectors have general preference requirements.
talent_foreign_worker_rule: Combined Expatriate Residence Permit and Alien Card required. Quota based on company capitalisation.
talent_key_consideration: Nigeria produces world class technology talent. Many diaspora professionals are returning creating a strong senior talent pipeline.

sector_priority_2_why: Chronic power deficit driving massive investment in off-grid solar, gas-to-power and grid infrastructure.

entry_step_4: Establish FX strategy — work with a tier 1 bank to structure USD accounts and repatriation arrangements upfront

name: Kenya

name: South Africa
main_industries: Mining · Finance · Manufacturing · Tourism · Agriculture
summary: Most industrialised African economy and gateway to continent
key_industry_1_desc: South Africa holds worlds largest reserves of platinum, manganese and chrome. Mining contributes 8% of GDP.
